item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00203","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C23","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.84,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C02 supplies the child’s central, concrete argument: while the steel parties are actively negotiating, outside governmental intervention could stop those negotiations and destroy the possibility of settlement. The child compresses and adapts that reasoning into a request that the Senate refrain from action that could alter the parties’ attitudes or cause negotiations to break down. C23 is also close because it addresses prospective Senate action in the same steel dispute and stresses the consequences of congressional intervention, but it advocates constructive legislation rather than noninterference during live bargaining. C06 parallels the emphasis on settlement by the parties, continued negotiations, and the national interest, but its requested action is an extension of operations rather than Senate restraint.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The parties to the dispute are now negotiating for a settlement of the dispute... any action by the Senate... could so alter the situation or the attitudes of the parties in this case as to cause a breakdown in their negotiations.","parent_excerpt":"A resort to the Taft-Hartley machinery during the time the parties were meeting, of course, would have stopped negotiations and destroyed any chance of settlement.","explanation":"Both make the same specific causal argument that governmental intervention while steel negotiations are underway could terminate bargaining and eliminate the prospect of settlement."},{"child_excerpt":"Everyone must agree that a settlement by the parties is by far the best thing that could happen in the national interest.","parent_excerpt":"I don't think it makes sense to use force when you can get cooperation by free consent.","explanation":"The child restates C02’s preference for a voluntary settlement by the disputing parties rather than imposed governmental action."}]}
